correctness.rationale: The two source half-sum involutes imply cyclic interpolation fractions \(t=(z/2a,x/2b,y/2c)\) and \(r=(x/2c,y/2a,z/2b)\). Their 3-by-3 product has equal off-diagonal entries in each column \((y^2/4ac,z^2/4ab,x^2/4bc)\) and row sums one, hence the displayed scalar-plus-rank-one identity. The center weights follow using \(Q=4abc-xyz\), and induction gives every iterate. Multiplying three arithmetic-geometric-mean inequalities proves \(\rho\le1/4\) with equality exactly \(x=y=z\). The family \(x=y=1,z\in(0,1]\) proves the complete positive range. Six exact-rational test families including asymmetric instances confirm all indices and five involute generations; no finite test substitutes the proof.
